Hi Sarah — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Privacy & Security counsel) and Rachel (your AE) to help move this along.

High level commitments: Redwood is happy to execute a DPA and standard contractual clauses for EU transfers. Our standard approach is:
- Execute the EU Commission SCCs (2010/2021 flow depending on counterparty request) and include our Appendix.
- For UK transfers, we usually attach the UK IDTA addendum (company signature) — we are willing to sign the customer-facing UK addendum for covered contracts.
- We maintain a public subprocessor registry and provide 30-day notice for any material additions; we'll provide the current list and last 12 months of changes.

That said, some of Acme's redlines touch on transfer-impact / onward transfer language and control over subprocessors; Monica will propose specific language we can accept or mark as explainable exceptions. If you have suggested limited transfer-impact wording, please paste it in the thread to save time.

Target: DocuSign sent by Thursday, final sign by next Tuesday. Does that timeline work?

Hi Sarah — Monica here from Redwood Legal. Thanks for the redlines; I reviewed the document and have attached a marked-up response (Redwood_DPA_Response_20260211.docx). Key points up front:

1) SCCs / Transfer mechanism
- We can execute the EU Commission SCCs (2021 modules) with our company-specific Appendix. We will include the SCC text and Appendix in the DocuSign envelope so the executed DPA contains the SCC binding text.

2) UK IDTA / Addendum
- We are prepared to sign the UK IDTA (addendum) as a mutually executed document alongside the DPA. Our standard UK addendum is included in the attached PDF (SCCs_and_UK_IDTA_Addendum.pdf). If Acme has a pre-signed UK addendum, we can accept your version subject to a short legal review.

3) Transfer Impact Assessments (TIA) / Impact language
- Redwood performs internal TIAs for customers upon request. We do not accept open-ended warranties about data adequacy; however, we will add a limited transfer-impact clause: we will notify customers of relevant authoritative guidance (e.g., EDPS/ICO updates) and collaborate on mitigation. See Section 6.4 in our redline (summary): "Redwood will provide reasonable cooperation and factual information for customer-specific transfer impact assessments; Customer remains responsible for legal assessment under applicable law."

4) Subprocessors
- We publish our subprocessor registry at https://www.redwood.com/subprocessors and provide 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors. We cannot grant pre-approval rights for every future subprocessor but can commit to advance notice and a remediation plan.

5) Audit & Data Subject Requests
- We accept SOC 2 Type II reports and will provide summary audit evidence on request. We cannot agree to on-site audits in production environments but will provide necessary evidence consistent with industry norms.

I highlighted concessions and sticky items in the redline. If Acme can accept the limited TIA language and our subprocessor notice process, I think we can proceed to DocuSign this week.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
